candidates.decision_summary: Task1 is high-quality. The original paper describes an observational election-level comparative study of Western democratic elections and discusses Hypothesis 4a: under SMD rules, party competition should lead the plurality winner close to the median voter. The authorized dataset has 331 election observations, 20 repeated country series, years 1945-2003, smd categories pr=244, smd=85, missing=2, and nonmissing continuous pldist1 ranging approximately 0 to 59. The code uses only the authorized Stata dataset; verifies smd, pldist1, and year; filters to smd/pr observations; drops only required missing focal fields; constructs smd_bin; estimates QuantReg pldist1 ~ smd_bin at q=0.5; and reports starting rows, exclusions, final rows, group summaries, coefficient, SE, p-value, CI, direction, and conclusion class. The median-regression model is a declared and justified robustness deviation from the anchor's mean-based regression/group-comparison reference; it preserves the same raw outcome, SMD-vs-PR contrast, full target population, time scope, and conclusion rule. This is not a semantic duplicate of Shared Memory path01 because path01 used OLS with decade fixed effects and country-clustered SEs for Task1, while this candidate estimates an unadjusted median contrast. No low-quality rule is triggered under M1-M6 or Task1 rules 1.1-1.9. Guardrails G1 and G14 are relevant: using a different but defensible model from the original/prior path is not by itself a defect. Verification limitation: I did not execute the analysis, as required by the pruning role.
